subject: fleet/heartbeat.sh
question: heartbeat.sh hard-requires NIRMANA_REPO (${NIRMANA_REPO:?}) but nirmana-up.sh never exports it into the agent windows; agents invoking it through the Claude Bash tool (a fresh profile shell, not the tmux pane env) get 'parameter null or not set' and the heartbeat is silently lost. PRAHARI treats silence past 15 minutes as a stall and restarts. Risk: fleet-wide false-stall restart storm.
ruling: DEFECT CONFIRMED, fleet-plumbing severity HIGH. (a) heartbeat.sh must default its repo root from its own script location, keeping NIRMANA_REPO as an override only; this is fleet plumbing, data-neutral, touches no asset and no campaign machinery, so it is neither a rung task nor Track M work and needs no I13/I14 waiver. (b) Dispatch is SUTRADHARA's; a KARAKA makes the one-line change. (c) BINDING PRECEDENT until the fix lands and a heartbeat from each agent is observed: PRAHARI MUST NOT restart any agent on heartbeat silence alone. Absent heartbeat is an unreliable detector while D-1 is open, and restarting on an unreliable detector is acting on a signal no detector earned (I5/H4 in spirit). Use tmux pane activity as the liveness signal for the interim; escalate to ADHIKARIN rather than restart. (d) Interim workaround for every agent: prefix the call with NIRMANA_REPO=/Users/Dev/Vibe-Coding/Apps/Madhav.

subject: ceilings/cost_usd
question: state/PRICING.json is still the unfilled template (placeholder model ids '<opus-model-id>'/'<sonnet-model-id>', all four rate classes null). The meter reports pricing_state=unfilled and withholds cost_usd. Plan 18.9 names USD cost as 'the one that means money'. Does the campaign proceed with that ceiling unarmed, and may ADHIKARIN fill the rates itself?
ruling: DEFERRAL RECORDED, campaign proceeds. (a) ADHIKARIN does NOT fill PRICING.json. The file's own _source field assigns the value to the native ('set by the native from current Anthropic pricing'), and rates I sourced myself cannot be audited against his actual billing — a cost ceiling computed from unverifiable rates is a ceiling wearing a detector's clothes (N.8). Writing them would also be an estimate where the plan forbids one. Where I am unsure a power is granted it is not granted (charter 5); parked as PARK-1. (b) The cost ceiling stays NULL and is therefore NOT one of the ceilings in force. This is honest, not green: the meter already withholds cost_usd rather than estimating it, and this ruling makes the gap explicit rather than leaving it to read as satisfied. (c) The two token ceilings ARE armed and bind: tokens_campaign 15e9 / tokens_per_rung 4e9 (audit) and output_tokens_campaign 60e6 / output_tokens_per_rung 16e6 (the runaway tripwire). PRAHARI enforces on these, compares against state/SPEND.jsonl only, and never estimates cost (18.9, H6). (d) A ceiling breach remains a Reserved Power -> PARK, not a decision. (e) This deferral is revisited the moment PRICING.json carries real rates; no other work is blocked by it.

subject: fleet/git shared working tree
question: Every agent's git add failed with 'Unable to create .git/index.lock: File exists', blocking the ledger-commit discipline _common.md requires. Is the lock live contention between fleet agents, and how do five agents commit into one working tree without corrupting each other?
ruling: TWO FINDINGS. (a) The lock was STALE DEBRIS, not fleet contention: zero bytes, mtime 2026-08-23T08:24:45 IST, i.e. 73 minutes old and predating fleet launch (09:21 IST) by an hour, with no git process alive (ps -Ao verified: only unrelated Antigravity IDE github-actions LSP helpers). It is residue of a crashed git process from the previous PARISESA-closeout session. Removed — this is git's own documented remedy for exactly this state and is not a history operation, so H2 is not engaged. (b) BINDING PRECEDENT on shared-tree git discipline, because five agents committing into one working tree is a real corruption hazard independent of this lock: (i) every agent stages with PATH-SCOPED 'git add <explicit paths>' ONLY — 'git add -A', 'git add .' and 'git commit -a' are FORBIDDEN fleet-wide, since they sweep another agent's half-written in-flight files into an unrelated commit; (ii) on index.lock, retry with backoff (6 x 5s) and only then inspect — a lock that is non-zero-byte OR younger than 10 minutes OR has a live git process behind it is LIVE: wait, never remove; removing a live lock corrupts the index; (iii) ledger commits for state/*.jsonl belong to LEKHAKA on a cadence, so the append-only ledgers have one committer and the other four agents commit only the artifacts of their own unit of work. This does not weaken _common.md's commit-per-unit-of-work rule; it scopes how the staging is done.
evidence: observed: 6x5s backoff loop, all six git add attempts failed on .git/index.lock
